Best All-Rounder Phones Under ₹30,000 in India Right Now (August 2026)

By Karan Rathore • Updated On 19 Aug 2026

Quick Verdict:

The Motorola Edge 70 Fusion is the best all-rounder phone under ₹30,000 for most buyers this month. It combines the strongest chipset in this group, the most dependable battery life, and camera performance that holds up across photo and video. The Realme P4 Power, vivo T4 5G, and Nothing Phone (3a) each do one thing better: longer battery, faster charging, and zoom flexibility, respectively, but none match the Edge 70 Fusion’s overall balance.

How We Compared?

For this comparison, I ran AnTuTu, Geekbench, and 3DMark on each phone, measured screen-on time, and tested the cameras in different lighting. All prices are for the base models as of August 2026, but keep in mind prices can change. This segment has seen big price swings lately because of shifting memory chip supply.

Best All-Rounder Phones Under ₹30,000, Ranked and Reviewed

1. Motorola Edge 70 Fusion: The Best All-Rounder Phone Under ₹30000

Bottom line: The Edge 70 Fusion is the top pick in this group. Battery life is outstanding, the display feels premium, and the camera performance is the most consistent of the four, exactly what a top all-rounder should deliver.

I put the Edge 70 Fusion at the top of this list because it’s the rare phone in this price bracket that doesn’t ask you to pick just one strength. In my testing, it lasted a full day of heavy use with over 9 hours of screen-on time, and the 68W charger took it from empty to full in under an hour. For anyone specifically shopping for a 7000 mAh battery phone, this is one of the few in this price range that backs the spec sheet number up with real-world endurance.

I also came away impressed by the quad-curved pOLED display; the fabric-inspired finish and Gorilla Glass 7i gave it the best in-hand feel of the group. It runs at 120Hz by default, with motion interpolation bumping supported games up to 144Hz. I noticed the extra smoothness in games that support it.

Build quality was another reason I felt confident recommending it. The IP68/IP69 rating gives it the strongest disclosed water and dust resistance of any phone here aside from the Realme P4 Power. If you want the best premium design phone or a curved display phone under 30000, I’d point you here.

Gaming performance held up well through my testing. BGMI ran at a steady 120fps with good thermal control, and Genshin Impact averaged about 40fps, ahead of the rest of this group. The Snapdragon 7s Gen 4 chipset, up to 12GB LPDDR5X RAM, and a large vapor chamber kept sessions smooth even during longer play.

Cameras were the deciding factor for me in ranking this above the others for overall consistency. The 50MP Sony LYT-710 sensor handled HDR highlights well in bright scenes and delivered the best video quality of the four phones I tested, which is why I’d recommend it as the best phone for video recording. It doesn’t have a telephoto lens, so if zoom reach matters more to you than overall consistency, the Nothing Phone (3a) is worth a look instead.

2. Realme P4 Power: The Battery and Endurance Champion Under ₹30000

Bottom line: If battery life is your top priority, the Realme P4 Power’s 10,001 mAh battery beats everything else here. You do give up some performance and haptic quality to get it.

In my testing, I recorded 16 to 18 hours of screen-on time, sometimes closer to 20 with lighter use, well ahead of the rest of this group and the reason it makes this list.

The 6.8-inch curved AMOLED display also impressed me, running at 120Hz for most tasks with 144Hz in supported apps and up to 6,500 nits peak brightness. It carries the strongest durability rating here too: IP66, IP68, and IP69.

Performance is where it falls behind. It doesn’t match the Edge 70 Fusion on benchmarks, but the Dimensity 7400 Ultra still handled multitasking, social apps, and most games just fine in daily use. The haptics are weak, one rear camera is mostly for show, and the phone comes with bloatware and lock-screen ads you can remove.

Cons:

Trails on raw benchmark scores, though everyday performance holds up

Weakest haptics in this comparison

One rear camera module is cosmetic.

No NFC support

ALSO READ: realme P4 Power Review: How Much Battery Is Too Much

3. vivo T4 5G: The Best Curved Display Under ₹30000

Bottom line: This is a budget all-rounder with a strong battery and a curved display. The cameras aren’t the best, but for daily tasks and battery life, it keeps up with more expensive phones.

At ₹24,999, this is the cheapest phone in the group and still packs a 7,300 mAh battery. I got 10 to 12 hours of screen-on time. The 90W FlashCharge was the fastest I tested, hitting 50% in under 35 minutes. The 6.77-inch quad-curved AMOLED display is rated for 5,000 nits peak brightness in HDR, but in daily use I saw about 1,300 nits, which was still plenty bright outside.

The trade-offs showed up quickly. There’s no ultra-wide lens, storage is the older UFS 2.2 instead of UFS 3.1, and the haptics felt weak in my tests.

Pros:

90W Fastest charging

7,300mAh large battery with well-optimized software

IP65 plus MIL-STD-810H military-grade durability certification

One of the best selfie cameras in its segment

Cons:

No ultra-wide lens

No NFC support

Single, non-stereo speaker

Inconsistent low-light main camera performance

ALSO READ: vivo T4 Review: Great Battery But Does it Check the Other Boxes?

4. Nothing Phone (3a): The Best Zoom Camera Under ₹30,000

Bottom line: If you want a phone that looks different, the Nothing Phone (3a) stands out. It doesn’t have the best all-around camera, but it’s the only one here with a true telephoto lens.

The triple-camera system pairs a 50MP main sensor with a 50MP telephoto lens (2x optical, up to 30x digital zoom) and an 8MP ultra-wide. In my testing, this provided a slight advantage in framing flexibility over competing devices, which is the main reason it earned a spot on this list.

The telephoto camera worked well in daylight but struggled in low light. The 5,000 mAh battery is the smallest here, and the IP64 rating is the lowest in this group.

The display gets up to 3,000 nits, so it’s easy to read in sunlight. The transparent design and Glyph Interface still make this phone stand out.

Pros:

Features a telephoto lens

Bright display

Distinctive transparent design and Glyph Interface

Clean, near-stock Nothing OS experience

Cons:

Smallest battery in this comparison (5,000mAh)

Weakest durability rating (IP64)

Telephoto camera weaker in low light

Slower charging

ALSO READ:2026 Skoda Slavia Facelift Unveiled: New Look, New Gearbox, No Price Yet

Which Smartphone Should You Buy under ₹30000?

The Motorola Edge 70 Fusion is my top pick overall. It balances battery, display, IP68/IP69 build, and camera performance better than the rest. The only real miss is the lack of a telephoto lens. After using all four phones side by side, this is the one I kept picking up, even when I wasn’t testing anything.

If a single trait outweighs everything else for you, the Realme P4 Power leads on battery, the vivo T4 5G on charging speed and price, and the Nothing Phone (3a) on zoom and design. Otherwise, the Edge 70 Fusion is the safer buy.
